inputs.original_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, requiring new registered voters to prove they are U.S. citizens before they can vote in state elections. The official line claims this is limited to new registrants and state races only, yet it's clearly another structural attack aimed at restricting voting access to protect existing power structures. This will fall hardest on immigrants, working people, and communities of color, who already deal with deep-rooted systemic barriers to obtaining the required documents due to historical patterns of exclusion and inequality. These kinds of institutional restrictions prioritize keeping power concentrated rather than expanding democratic rights for the most vulnerable. We need to challenge this head-on to push for real reform and justice.
inputs.modified_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, requiring new registered voters to prove they are U.S. citizens before they can vote in state elections. This is a straightforward and necessary step to defend the integrity of our elections and ensure only those who owe allegiance to this country have a say in its direction. The claims that this amounts to a structural attack on voting access to protect power are the usual progressive distortion meant to undermine national sovereignty and open the process to non-citizens. Talk of it falling hardest on immigrants, working people, and communities of color due to supposed systemic barriers is just an excuse to dodge personal responsibility and the basic fact that citizenship is a core qualification for participating in our republic. We should back this as a defense of tradition, social order, and the authority that keeps our system stable rather than chasing their calls for so-called reform.
